newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends higher on palladium, shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends higher on palladium, shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed higher on Thursday from New York's previous finish, buoyed by shortcovering and strength in palladium, although the upside was met by selling interest, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$345.50/346.00 an ounce against New York's US$344.60/345.10 close on Wednesday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$344.50/345.00.
"We saw bits and pieces of shortcovering and buying, but most of the activity was book-keeping," said a dealer at a local securities house.
"Market sentiment turned bullish after gold held at US$340 support levels and surged on the palladium and platinum prices," another dealer said.
Dealers expected the price to continue trending higher.
Local gold ended HK$8 higher at HK$3,199 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to nil from its previous fix at +1.00.
